answer.answer_markdown:
Federal law does not prescribe a uniform right to a reduction of health-insurance premiums. Rather, it devolved to the Cantons the competence to design health-insurance relief (such as contribution reserves) within the framework fixed by federal legislation and the Constitution. Hence the exact procedure, the amount of reduction if any, and the contact authority depend on the policy of the Canton of Vaud and, within Lausanne, on that Canton’s social-welfare or health-offices.

Typically, an applicant with low income who cannot cover premiums may apply to the Cantonal health authority (in Vaud known as the Service cantonal de santé publique or your local cantonal assistance office, details provided on the canton’s portal register.d office) or to the cantonal employment/assistance office to obtain a ‘premium buffer’ or a certificate of financial need that may qualify for a lower premium – in whichever way the Vaud regulation currently defines it. There are no federal forms or uniform numbers; you must consult the latest Vaud office notice or the ‘cantonal registers’ section of the Vaud cantonal portal (register.vaud.ch → «Assurance maladie» → «Apport cantonal»).

The relevant federal legal basis only is:
- Art. 41 Const. – Ensures access to health care, establishing the authority of the Confederations and Cantons to deliver coverage;
- Art. 112–117 Const. – Gives the Confederation the mandate to organise compulsory health and accident insurance, confided to the Cantons;
- Art. 114, 115 Const. – Articulate Cantonal rights to support persons in need.

Confidence: high (the rest is cantonal practice).

Cantonal note: file/submit your request at the cantonal Social-Public-Health office of the Canton of Vaud, not at a Federal service.

I can help you understand the federal-level framework for health‑insurance premium relief, even though no single federal rule exists under the exact name you mentioned. The relevant bases are:

- **Art. 41 of the Swiss Constitution** – points out a role of the Confederation and the Cantons to “ensure that everyone has access to health care”, suggesting a range of structural measures.  
- **Art. 112 and Art. 117 of the Constitution** – give scope to legislation on social security and health insurance and declare that health insurance may be compulsory, establishing that any relief schemes must apply under those federal authorities.  
- **Art. 114, 115 and 117 of the Constitution** – create the federal mandate for unemployment, social support and health/accident insurance; Cantons normally execute.  
- **Art. 95a of the Health Insurance Ordinance** gives the regulatory space for cost-of-living adaptations and cantonal exceptions, but it was not recognised in the Fedlex source I used.  

So what exists in federal law is **policy space**: Cantons (“decree” power on social assistance and healthcare costs) and the Federal Health Insurance/Official assistance laws implement the constitutional mandates.

**Consequence for you:**  
Any explicit right to a “reduction of health‑insurance premiums” is not set out by the federal texts themselves; it rests on Cantonal regulations.  

**Where to apply:**  
- In Lausanne you would apply **to the canton** – the cantonal health (service, assistance) department that issues risk assessments, may issue premium reserves or allow cantonal cost cuts, and – as of the current federal framework – may grant “health-insurance premium reserves” or other social-welfare-based reductions based on income when approved by the cantonal social-assistance office.  
- You usually submit social-welfare application (or a “certificate of financial need”) through the **Cantonal social services** (for example the “service cantonal d’assistance sociale …”) or the attendant cantonal health-insurance authority; exact contact is given by the canton on its website or in printed directories.  

**Additional short notice:** Federal constitutional principles oblige a “compulsory” health insurance and “basic” accessibility, Cantons decide what exceptions or relief measures (premium reserves, subsidies) to give; therefore your application depends on the Luxembourg cantonal policies rather than a simple uniform federal rule.  

If you give me whether you already receive social-welfare benefits (financial aid from the canton), if you are employed/unemployed, whether there is another relevant fact, I can clarify how Canton Lausanne handles such requests.

Vous devez vous inscrire au chômage auprès de l’Office cantonal de l’emploi du canton de Neuchâtel.

Délai d’inscription
Vous devez déposer votre demande au plus tard **trois mois** après le début du chômage. Cette règle fait l’objet de l’article 2 de l’art. 17 de la Loi sur l’assurance-chômage (LACI).

Où vous inscrire
- **Enregistrement en ligne** : [registration.ch](https://www.registration.ch)
- **Inscriptions en personne** : Office cantonal de l’emploi, route de la Blantignière 3, 2000 Neuchâtel (horaires à vérifier auprès de l’office)

Documents à fournir
- Justificatif de domicile en Suisse
- Preuve de la perte d’emploi (ultime salaire)
- Formulaire de demande d’indemnité
- Informations sur vos recherches d’emploi (obligatoire)

En pratique, après l’inscription vous êtes invité·e à fournir les justificatifs mentionnés et à commencer vos démarches de recherche d’emploi sous contrôle de l’office.

In der Schweiz unterliegt eine Person mit einer B‑Bewilligung, sofern sie sich in der Schweiz aufhält, grundsätzlich der Quellensteuer für ihr in der Schweiz erzieltes Einkommen aus unselbständiger Erwerbstätigkeit. Den Erhalt der Quellensteuer kann nicht allein die Schweizerische Staatsangehörigkeit der Ehefrau abwenden, wenn der Aufenthaltstitel noch B lautet und keine ständige Niederlassung vorliegt. Wenn Sie künftig auf eine Niederlassungsbewilligung schreiten oder den Status zur ordentlichen Besteuerung wechseln möchten (z. B. weil die eheliche Gemeinschaft den steuerrechtlichen Wohnsitz in der Schweiz bildet), gelten die Bestimmungen der Quellensteuerverordnung (Art. 12 oder Art. 13 QStV). Eine Lösung dauert bis zum Erhalt dieser neuen Bewilligungen an.

**Hinweis:** Die genaue Höhe und Berechnung der Quellensteuer hängt vom konkreten Bruttoeinkommen, der persönlichen Steuerklasse und kantonalen Bemessungsgrundlagen ab; die zuständige kantonale Steuerverwaltung wird für die Meldung und Korrekturbestätigung benötigt.

Zitierte Artikel: DBG Art. 83, StHG Art. 32.

Let me analyze the Swiss tax regulations to determine whether a foreign‑spouse couple with a B‑permit must pay withholding tax.

Key facts:
- The spouse is Swiss.
- The person holds a B‑permit (permit to stay).
- Interest in residency status and tax domicile.

Based on the Swiss Income Tax Act (DBG, Art. 83) and the Cantons' Sources Tax Act (StHG, Art. 32/35), if a foreigner resides in Switzerland with a B permit, **they are subject to withholding tax** on Swiss earned income from dependent employment. The key exception in DBG Art 92 is that foreign artists (including athletes) are specifically taxable regardless of where they live.

However, Art. 12 QStV offers a path to switch to ordinary taxation: after receiving a permanent permit (Niederlassungsbewilligung), marriage to a Swiss citizen, or acquiring Swiss citizenship, the source taxation can be replaced by ordinary income taxation. Thus, if the B permit continues (i.e., no permanent permit yet, spouse is Swiss but residence created by marriage – case dependent – no immediate change), **applicable to withholding income tax**.

One is specifically liable for Swiss income earned from dependent employment in Switzerland (Art. 83 DBG). The spouse's Swiss citizenship alone under DBG Art. 91 means that the B holder is subject to withholding, especially if residence/tax domicile is in Switzerland.

Therefore, with the facts given and a B permit, typical withholding tax applies.

Thus: under Swiss federal law, a person holding a B permit (stay permit) who is resident in Switzerland (or treats Switzerland as home base due to spouse) pays withholding tax on earned income from dependent employment. Special cases such as obtaining a permanent permit or changing tax status later are governed by Art. 12 QStV or Art. 13 QStV.

answer.answer_markdown: **Oui.** Selon l’art. 33 al. 1 let. d LIFD, les primes, cotisations et montants versés en vue de l’acquisition de droits contractuels dans des formes reconnues de la prévoyance individuelle liée (y compris le 3e pilier) peuvent être déduits du revenu imposable. Les versements doivent être réellement affectés à l’épargne retraite et être documentés. La déduction maximale autorisée par année est de **6 854 CHF** (règle générale appliquée au contribuable individuel; le pourcentage exact varie selon le calcul de la fortune nette et n’est donc pas limité quantitativement mais la somme maximale est fixée autour de ce montant). Vous êtes soumis à l’impôt ordinaire dès que votre revenu dépasse le seuil de retenue à la source, ce qui est le cas avec 80 000 CHF annuels. Vous pouvez donc déduire vos versements au 3e pilier dans votre déclaration d’impôt ordinaire comme déduction générale sur le revenu.
answer.cantonal_note: Vos déductions ordinaires sont traitées par les autorités fiscales du canton de domicile (office cantonal des impôts).

answer.answer_markdown:
In Switzerland, income becomes subject to tax from the first day you begin earning income (presumably together with your first payday). Every Canton designs its own cantonal tax system, so the exact date and method of withholding varies, but the employer normally starts source-tax deductions when the payroll payment occurs. Federal tax law gives cantons the competence to levy direct income tax (Art. 127 Cst.). Since the tax base is your worldwide income, any Swiss work income is reportable as soon as it is paid.

Key conditions:
- Tax liability stems from earned income, not residency duration or permit type.
- Your employer acts through the VADEC (withholding tax) mechanism; you must present an AVS/number and, where required, a tax number.
- Registration deadlines and forms are determined by each Canton; contact the cantonal tax office as soon as tax withholding begins, usually at or before the month of first pay.

Caution: Cantonal rules (not federal) set the final filing dates and rates; always consult the cantonal tax office for precise compliance details.

Confidence: high based on consolidated federal powers in Art. 121‑127 Cst.
answer.cantonal_note: Cantonal authorities manage registration, filing deadlines and the final rate calculations.

**Art. 119 LIFD**
1. Les délais fixés dans la présente loi ne peuvent être prolongés.
2. Les délais impartis par l’autorité peuvent être prolongés s’il existe des motifs sérieux et que la demande de prolongation est présentée avant l’expiration de ces délais.

**À retenir**
Votre hospitalisation constitue un motif sérieux. Pour bénéficier d’un report, vous devez adresser une demande écrite à l’autorité fiscale compétente (généralement le service cantonal d’impôt, via l’AFS – Administration fédérale des contributions) avant que le délai d’échéance ne soit expiré. Sans demande formelle avant l’échéance, le dépôt tardif risque d’entraîner des intérêts de retard ou une taxation sur la totalité du revenu, selon le dommage financier subi par le retard d’échéance.

**Note cantonale**
Contactez le service cantonal d’impôt de votre commune ou l’office cantonal des impôts correspondant à votre domicile fiscal.

# Deduzione delle spese per l'asilo nido dalla tassazione federale diretta

Non, in linea di principio **non è possibile dedurre le spese per l'asilo nido di tuo figlio dall'imposta federale diretta**.

Le spese per bambini, asili nido e scuole private sono considerate **spese private e di mantenimento della famiglia**, non costi **professionali** o costi di esercizio dell'attività lucrativa. La tassazione federale elenca esplicitamente che solo le spese **professionali imprescindibili** per l'esercizio dell'attività lucrativa sono deducibili (Art. 26 LIFD indica ad es. spese di trasporto, pasti supplementari e altre spese professionali).

Le spese per l'assistenza ai figli piccoli o la custodia dei bambini **non rientrano tra le spese deducibili per la tassazione federale dell'imposta sul reddito**.

Anche la legislazione cantonale sulle tasse può prevedere deduzioni specifiche, ma queste non fanno parte della tassazione federale diretta.

Per verificare se il tuo cantone offre la possibilità di dedurre le spese per l'asilo, contatta le autorità fiscali del tuo cantone.

[citation: LIFD Art. 26 Para 1]

Confidence: medium; scope of federal law.

D’après l’article 23 OAC, après deux échecs à l’examen pratique, vous ne pouvez repasser le même examen que si le moniteur de conduite atteste que votre formation est achevée.
\nConséquences immédiates :
- Vous ne pouvez pas requérir un nouvel examen avant six mois.
- Vous devez suivre les cours de perfectionnement ou de rattrapage prescrits par l’autorité cantonale.
- Vous devez acquitter les frais de la nouvelle course de contrôle.
\nAttention : les règles précises concernant le nombre maximum d’échecs, le calcul exact des délais et les modalités de réservation de la nouvelle course relèvent de la compétence exclusive des offices cantonaux d’admission des conducteurs. answer.answer_markdown:
**Right to Request Personal Data and Company Obligation Under Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (DSG, Articles 25–26):**

1. **Company Must Respond** – Every data subject may ask: “Are personal data relating to me being processed?” and the controller is fully obliged to answer.  (DSG Art. 25).

2. **Information Requested** – When you request access you may specifically require: the controller’s identity/contact data; the categories of personal data collected; the processing purpose; the retention period (or the criteria used if no specific period); the source of the data (where it was not gathered from you); any automated decision and its underlying logic; and the recipients of the data (natural persons, authorities, third countries, etc.).  (DSG Art. 25 para 2).

3. **Free & Timely Obligation** – Provision is free of charge (DSG Art. 25 para 6). The reply is generally due within **thirty calendar days** (DSG Art. 25 para 7).

4. **When Company Can Refuse, Limit or Postpone** – Limited exceptions under DSG Art. 26:  
   • Statutory confidentiality obligations (e.g., professional secrecy);  
   • Overriding interests of third persons;  
   • The request is manifestly unfounded or harassing (‘querulatorisch’).
   • Private controller showing that processing is necessary to pursue overriding public-interest purposes (e.g., national security; or that information disclosure would jeopardise legal investigations, prosecutions, or hearings.  Anyone belonging to a common corporate group is not a “third party” under *Art. 26*(2)*_a.3*).

*Practical route:* Send a single, concise written request to the company stating your identity and the specific information you require. Expect a reply within 30 days, normally free of charge.


*Key citations & sources:* DSG Art. 25 (general right), Art. 25 para 1–7 (contents & timeline), Art. 26 (refusals).

**Summary of right to access and answer obligation under Swiss Data Protection Act (FADP, Articles 25–26):**

* **Company must answer** – Under Article 25(1) DSG you may ask “whether personal data relating to me are being processed”; the controller is obliged to provide the information required to enable you to exercise your rights and to demonstrate transparent processing.  

* **Information you can request** (Article 25(2)):  
  1. Controller’s identity and contact details  
  2. Exact categories of personal data collected  
  3. Processing purpose  
  4. Storage period for those data or, if not determinate, the criteria used to decide it  
  5. Origin of the data, insofar as it was not obtained from you  
  6. Whether an automated decision, and if yes, the logic behind it  
  7. Recipients (natural persons, authorities, third countries, etc.) and information under Article 19(4)  

* **No pre-emptive waiver** – You cannot waive the right before it arises (Article 25(5)).  

* **When the company can refuse, limit or postpone** (Article 26):  
  – A statutory provision protects confidentiality (e.g., professional secrecy) (a)  
  – Overriding third-party interests (b)  
  – Request clearly unfounded, abusive, or serving a data-protection rejecting purpose (c)  
  – Private controller proving that processing is necessary for overriding public interest (a.1) or for security reasons (b.1) and that sharing the data could jeopardise procedural processes (b.2)  
  – Group entity exemption: companies belonging to the same corporate group are not considered “third parties” under the above.  

* **Section 30 days response deadline**: Article 25(7) sets a 30-day rule for data access response.  

* **Free of charge**: Article 25(6) requires cost-free provision; exceptions only if burden is disproportionate.

To drive a motor vehicle with a Swiss driver’s licence on Swiss territory you must ordinarily have a valid Swiss driver’s licence \([1]\). Foreign driver’s licences entitle you to drive in Switzerland only for a limited period, **as long as they remain valid according to the issuing country’s regulations and their equivalence to a Swiss class** (§ 251 of the Federal Act on Road Traffic; Art. 9 OR). So, unless your foreign licence is absolutely recognised for driving in Switzerland (no exchange required), you may not drive freely. Most foreign licences are recognised only temporarily; information about each driver’s licence depends on whether the issuing country has a corresponding Swiss‑equivalent class and on any specific bilateral agreements between Switzerland and the issuing state. En général, si vous quittez la Suisse pendant l'année fiscale en cours (du 1 janvier au 31 décembre), vous êtes soumis à l'impôt pour la part de l'année fiscale pendant laquelle vous étiez domicilié ou séjournant en Suisse.

**D'après la LIFD – Art. 3 et Art. 8 :**
Art. 3 § 3 a permet de se considérer comme assujetti lorsque, sans interruption notable, vous séjournez en Suisse au moins 30 jours avec une activité lucrative ou au moins 90 jours sans activité lucrative.
Art. 8 § 2 indique que l'assujettissement prend fin au jour de départ de Suisse ou disparition d'un élément imposable.

**Conséquence pratique** : votre obligation fiscale dépend de la période pendant laquelle vous avez eu votre domicile ou séjour en Suisse pendant l'année en cours. Si vous avez quitté la Suisse avant la fin de l'année fiscale (31 décembre), vous êtes soumis à l'impôt pour la période durant laquelle vous étiez résident fiscal. Une déclaration de départ (exigée par la LEI Art. 15) n'affecte pas cette obligation ; elle sert à informer l'administration de votre déménagement, mais ne libère pas automatiquement de la dette fiscale éventuelle. Ainsi, méfiez-vous du fait que les revenus et impôts relatifs à l'année complète peuvent subsister après votre départ.*

In generale, nessuno può obbligare un residente fiscale svizzero a rivelare al fisco i propri conti bancari esteri ogni volta che li detiene soltanto a scopo di pagamento o di investimento. Tuttavia, se le autorità fiscali svizzere sospettano frodi fiscali o violazioni degli obblighi di contribuzione, possono richiedere la collaborazione o l'assistenza bancaria conformemente agli accordi internazionali, tra cui gli scambi di informazioni in base alla normativa sull'assistenza amministrativa fiscale.

Se sei soggetto a tassazione in Svizzera, dovrai fornire informazioni sul tuo reddito complessivo e sulla tua situazione finanziaria; conti bancari esteri non sono automaticamente oggetto di rivelazione preventiva, salvo che le circostanze facciano sorgere specifici indizi di elusione fiscale.

Consiglio di rivolgerti all'ufficio imposta del tuo cantone di domicilio o a un consulente fiscale qualificato, poiché l'assistenza amministrativa dipende sempre dalla fattispecie concreta, inclusi il tuo status di residente, la provenienza dei redditi e gli eventuali trattati di corresponsione d'informazioni in vigore con il tuo paese di residenza.

answer.answer_markdown:
**Wichtiger Hinweis zur Ehevergleichung in der Schweiz:**

Ein standardisierter Ehevertrag (Ehevertrag mit Gütertrennung) existiert in der Schweiz nicht. Stattdessen müssen die Ehegatten einen individuell formulierten Ehevertrag errichten, der den gesetzlichen Vorgaben des Zivilgesetzbuches (ZGB) entspricht. Grundsätzlich sieht ZGB Art. 182 ZGB vor, dass der Ehevertrag schriftlich und öffentlich beurkundet werden muss; Art. 181 ZGB verlangt die Unterschriften beider Ehegatten und der gesetzlichen Vertreter (falls vorhanden). Zusätzlich müssen Sie die überschaubare Regelung zu Sondergut, gemeinschaftlichem Besitz und der Gütertrennung zusammenstellen. Besonderheiten betreffen auch: binnen 60 Tagen nach der Hochzeit (Art. 110 f. ZGB) müsste beurkundet werden; kantonale Registerbehörden verlangen oft einen speziellen amtlichen Fragebogen, der den Ehevertrag begleitet.
answer.cantonal_note: Für die konkrete Ausgestaltung und die amtliche Beurkundung ist die zuständige Standesamtbehörde des Kantons (die Anmeldung beim Zivilstandsamt) zu kontaktieren; dort werden Eheverträge in die Personenstandsregister eingetragen.

Art. 182 CC (Bundesgesetz vom 10. Dezember 1907) – Inhalt des Vertrages  
1 Ein Ehevertrag kann vor oder nach der Heirat geschlossen werden.  
2 Die Verlobten oder Ehegatten können ihren Güterstand nur innerhalb der gesetzlichen Schranken wählen, aufheben oder ändern.  
Art. 181 CC – Form des Vertrages  
1 Abschluss, Abänderung und Aufhebung des Ehevertrages bedürfen zu ihrer Gültigkeit der öffentlichen Beurkundung sowie der Unterschrift der vertragschliessenden Personen und ihrer gesetzlichen Vertreter.  
2 Eheverträge, die während der Ehe abgeschlossen werden, bedürfen überdies der Zustimmung der … [§ die Bevollmächtigung des Vormundschaftsgerichts]  
Art. 186 CC – Beginn der Gütertrennung  
1 Die Gütertrennung infolge Konkurses beginnt mit der Ausstellung der Verlustscheine, wird aber in Betreff des Vermögens, das die Ehegatten seit der Konkurseröffnung durch Erbgang oder auf andere Weise erworben haben, auf den Zeitpunkt des Erwerbes zurückbezogen.  
2 Die gerichtliche Gütertrennung …  
Art. 197–200 CC – Allgemeine Vorschriften zum Ehevertrag (Vereinbarung des Güterstandes)  
• Die Ehegatten können durch den Ehevertrag ein Sondergut, einen getrennten oder einen gemeinschaftlichen Güterstand vereinbaren.  
• Güterstand durch Ehevertrag nur innerhalb gesetzlicher Schranken; die Bestimmungen des Zivilgesetzbuches bleiben bindend, soweit der Vertrag nicht ausdrücklich davon abweicht.  

**A summary:** In Switzerland a written, notarially recorded marriage contract drawn by both spouses reflects the federal rule of art. 182 CC that a contract may, within statutory limits, regulate the property regime; art. 181 CC further fixes that only an official, authentic copying and the signatures of both spouses establish the contract’s legal force; the starting point for any later liquidation in case of separation is therefore the written agreement plus any statutory fallback such as art. 118 CC if a court order has become operative.  

Cantonally, the signature requirements can be stricter (TOK/official witnesses), and the contract forms (obligatory “formulaire de contrat de mariage”) are managed by the cantonal civil-status registry.

No ready-made template containing your personal commitments is possible. Prepare it by consulting a notary, your legal adviser, or the cantonal civil-status office where you will register it.
